paraphrase: Strong version: for every sentence, if it is meaningful (literally, cognitively significant), so is its negation.

self_evident.note: Floor item approved by the owner on 2026-11-05 (#1008) on the common-ground basis; strong version. It is the weakest version the strengthened 1946 corollary (AYER-1946-EXCLUDES-A-NEGATION-FAILS) needs, since that rival says only that some negated sentence is excluded, so closure must hold at an arbitrary sentence. Defeat 2 needs only the weak version (STMT-MEANINGFULNESS-CLOSED-UNDER-NEGATION-WEAK), which this entails (MEANING-NEGATION-CLOSURE-STRONG-ENTAILS-WEAK). Hempel imposes the biconditional (S meaningful iff its negation is) as an adequacy condition, as SEP reports him; this is its left-to-right half. The recorded rival stays recorded and unrefuted, and the common-ground criterion is not mechanically met, so the premise is established relative to the owner's approval.
